newsitem.title: USA: UAL sees dilution from Galileo deal.
newsitem.headline: UAL sees dilution from Galileo deal.

text.p: UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, said Wednesday it expects slight dilution from the Galileo International Partnership deal but expects to make up for that reduction in earnings with its airline operations.

A UAL spokeman declined to comment on the amount of dilution that is expected to result from the agreement, announced late Tuesday, for Galileo to buy United's 77 percent interest in Apollo Travel Services.
In addition, Galileo, which is 38 percent owned by United, plans an initial public offering.

Goldman Sachs analyst Glenn Engel said he estimated dilution from the Galileo deal would be about $0.20 to $0.25 a share. This compares with the current First Call mean estimate for fiscal 1997 of $9.12 a share, based on a range of $7.61 to $10.01.
"United...will make up for (dilution from the deal) on operations. The airline business continues better than expected," Engel said.
Gruntal & Co analyst Steven Lewins applauded the Galileo deal, adding he did not expect the stock to react to any dilution concerns.

"United (shares won't) go up or down from dilution on this. I think they will use the money much more intelligently within the airline to get a higher rate of return," Lewins said. "From a portfolio standpoint, I think it's a brilliant decision."
UAL shares were off 1/4 at 79-5/8 after trading as high as 81-3/8, a new 52-week high, earlier this morning.
As announced late Tuesday, Galileo, which is owned by 11 airlines including United, agreed to buy Apollo Travel Services Partnership, another computer reservation system, for $700 million.
United will receive $539 million for its 77 percent stake in Apollo.
Analysts said possible uses for the cash United will receive include to retire additional debt or purchase aircraft.
"They may continue to boost the balance sheet or buy back debt or use it as fund for aircraft," Furman Selz fixed income analyst Raymond Neidl analyst said.
Other owners in Apollo are US Airways Group Inc, with a 21 percent stake, and Air Canada, with a two percent interest.
As announced Tuesday, Galileo's airline owners will each retain an ownership interest in Galileo after the initial public offering.
United has said it does not plan to sell any of its shares of Galileo as part of the offering and expects to retain a significant ownership percentage.
Galileo provides travel agencies and other subscribers with the ability to access airline schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines.
